name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, a pine-covered hill station at about 1,500 m elevation known as the Scotland of the East. Colonial architecture, markets, lakes, and base for exploring Khasi Hills attractions.

name: Jowai
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district and cultural-commercial hub of the Pnar (Jaintia) people on a plateau at about 1,380 m elevation, encircled by the Myntdu River. Base for exploring Nartiang, Thadlaskein, Krang Suri and the southern Umngot circuit.
facts: HQ of West Jaintia Hills district

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning multi-stream waterfall near Amlarem dropping into a crystal-clear turquoise pool surrounded by limestone cliffs and dense forest. One of Meghalaya’s most photogenic falls; short trek to the base where swimming is possible in season.
facts: Located near Amlarem, about 30 km from Jowai

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest concentration of megalithic standing stones (menhirs and dolmens) in Meghalaya, north of Nartiang market. Erected between the 16th and 19th centuries by Jaintia clans and kings; tallest menhir about 8 m. Summer capital remnant of the Jaintia kingdom.

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: 600-year-old Shakti Peeth dedicated to Goddess Jayanti (Durga) in Nartiang village. One of the 51 Shakti Peethas where Sati’s left thigh is believed to have fallen; major pilgrimage site especially during Durga Puja.

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Man-made historical lake (Pung Sajar Nangli) beside NH-6 near Mukhla village, about 8 km from Jowai. Legend says it was dug by the bows of Sajar Nangli and his followers; popular picnic and boating spot amid pine-fringed hills.

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town on the crystal-clear Umngot River famous for glass-like water where boats appear to float in air. India-Bangladesh border crossing with historic suspension bridge; gateway for Shnongpdeng and Jaflong views.

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Quiet riverside village a few kilometres upstream from Dawki on the Umngot, popular for kayaking, snorkelling, cliff jumping, camping and homestays. Less crowded alternative to Dawki with clear water and forested hills.

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tiered waterfall about 5–8 km from Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai road, cascading over rocks into a pool amid paddy fields. Accessible via a short walk across an arch bridge; lesser-known alternative to more famous falls.

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai with sacred grove, manicured lawns and panoramic views over the Pynthor Wah valley and Myntdu River. Developed for nature walks, picnics and birdwatching.

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Riverside area on the Myntdu River meaning ‘golden flower’, with calm pools, suspension bridge, paddy fields and the U Kiang Nangbah memorial. Historic site of the Jaintia freedom movement and popular local picnic ground.

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered secluded waterfall in Amlarem sub-division with a clear blue plunge pool, reached by a moderate trek through forest. Paradise Adventure Camp nearby; quieter alternative to Krang Suri.

name: Thlu Muwi (Megalithic Bridge)
description: Historic megalithic stone bridge built over the Muwi stream by Jaintia warriors, about 16 km from Jowai on the Dawki road. Used by kings travelling between Sylhet and the summer capital at Nartiang; adjacent waterfall.
facts: About 16 km from Jowai on Dawki road
